findings.reason: the section must name the dry-run call site as the second threader (it is already in the write paths), or a node that follows the brief exactly lands a change that refuses a valid preview.
findings.text: §3 says `plan_dispatch` "calls it with the two values as new parameters, which `dispatch()` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py` near line 1670) threads through from the CLI", but the dry-run branch calls `plan_dispatch` directly at `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1917` with its own argument list and never enters `dispatch()`, so implementing exactly as written leaves that caller passing the empty defaults and `crew dispatch --dry-run --brief ... --plan-link <slug>` is refused as though no link were given — §5 of the same plan already records that the dry run calls `plan_dispatch` at that line, so the omission is inside the plan's own evidence

— the four negative controls are numbered against a five-case list, so read literally "not reading `dispatch_options` makes the third case refuse" names the third case (`one with --plan-link is stored with the link in dispatch_options`), which is a dispatch-time storage assertion that landing-side reading cannot affect, and "treating a missing recorded link as a discharge makes the fourth case pass" names the fourth case (`its landing discharge passes with no landing flag`), which already passes and so cannot be falsified by that mutation — the mutations are right but their numbers are one list-position off from the cases they can falsify (the fifth case is the one that must stop being refused); WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: a worker following the numbered controls to the letter runs a mutation against a case it cannot change, and either reports an unreachable control or reshapes the test to make the number fit.

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3's five done-when cases are each failable and measurable, but its four negative controls are numbered "the third case" and "the fourth case" against that five-item list, and the natural reading of both numbers names a case the stated mutation cannot affect.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §3 puts every log under the run directory, starting with its revision and the literal command and ending in `EXIT=`, so nothing lands in a scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.

rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 carries one deliverable: the brief run's plan link and unplanned reason are asked for and recorded at dispatch, and the landing discharge reads the recorded value.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §3's wait on §2 is declared in `plan-section-depends-on` (`{"s3": ["a-refusal-comes-before-the-work#s2"]}`) and restated in the section, and the three files it shares are in §2's write paths, so no needed dependency is missing and no relationship points at the wrong node.
